quarterly_data.quarter: Generate Biomedicines press release: Roswell Park, Generate Biomedicines Launch Exclusive (10-01-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center and Generate announced on October 1, 2026 that the first patient has been dosed in the first-in-human Phase 1 trial (NCT07489287) of GB-5267, an investigational autologous IL-18 armored CAR T-cell therapy targeting MUC16 (over-expressed by more than 80% of ovarian tumors), in ovarian cancer, recruiting patients whose disease has returned after treatment or does not respond to platinum-based chemotherapy, the standard first-line treatment; the trial, led by Principal Investigator Emese Zsiros at Roswell Park, evaluates safety and tolerability and is enrolling. Each patient's T cells are collected, genetically engineered and expanded in Roswell Park's GMP Engineering & Cell Manufacturing Facility. The study requires no lymphodepletion chemotherapy and delivers the cells both intravenously and into the peritoneal cavity. Generate engineered GB-5267 with AI by designing and evaluating CAR architectures at scale based on how T cells actually behave rather than on binding affinity, optimizing potency, proliferation and persistence; the release calls it the first next-generation cell therapy for ovarian cancer to enter clinical trials (company claim). Dinesh de Alwis, SVP and Head of Clinical Drug Development: dosing the first patient 'begins the clinical test of whether that function-first approach behaves in patients as intended.'
